hero.prompt: Hero banner for an open-source developer tool called CUSTOMS AUTHORITY. Left third: a round official navy customs seal top-left reading 'CUSTOMS AUTHORITY' around the rim with a small crest of a stamp and a checkmark inside; beneath it a very large bold wordmark 'CUSTOMS AUTHORITY' in navy with a clean subtitle line 'DEPARTMENT OF SNAP JUDGMENTS', and a short tagline in a gold button: 'FAST LANE FOR THE SURE. SECONDARY FOR THE REST.' Center: Frankie404 (see mascot spec) dressed as a friendly customs officer — a navy peaked officer's cap with gold trim and a small gold stamp emblem resting on his cream dome, a small officer's epaulette on his techwear — standing at a cream-and-navy customs inspection booth, one hand raised in a welcoming wave, the other holding a big rubber stamp. Right: two clearly labeled lanes leading away from the booth: a green-sage fast lane with an overhead sign 'CLEARED' where small document cards flow through quickly each carrying a gold stamped checkmark, and a second lane with an overhead sign 'SECONDARY INSPECTION' where a few document cards with a coral question mark are gently routed to a calm desk with a lamp. Subtle background: a stylized border checkpoint with a barrier arm and a small 'DECISIONS INBOUND' flag. Bottom navy bar with four small icon+label features: OPEN SOURCE, EVERY DECISION STAMPED, ESCALATES WHEN UNSURE, BUILT IN COMMUNITY. No install commands, no version numbers, no URLs, no percentages anywhere in the image.

how-it-works.prompt: Clean modern 4-step horizontal infographic on a deep navy (#1E2A4A / #2B3A67) background, flat-vector style with paper grain, one warm coral accent, sunshine-yellow and gold highlights, crisp white sans-serif labels. Title across the top in white: 'HOW IT WORKS'. Four evenly spaced steps left to right connected by a thin dotted cream line, each a simple bold icon inside a cream rounded card with a one-word title and a short caption. Step 1 FIND: a magnifying glass over a flowchart with one node glowing yellow, caption 'spot the decisions hiding in your pipeline'. Step 2 WRITE: a form sheet with a multiple-choice question and short criteria lines under each option, one line highlighted coral, caption 'write the questions, with criteria'. Step 3 CHECK: a scoreboard clipboard next to an answer-key sheet with green checkmarks and one coral cross, caption 'prove it against your answer key'. Step 4 SHIP: a small customs booth with two lanes, a gold stamp marked CLEARED on the fast lane and a small sign SECONDARY on the other, caption 'stamp the sure, escalate the rest'. Frankie404 (see mascot spec) in a customs officer cap, small, in the bottom-right corner, pointing at step 4 with a friendly presenting gesture. Minimal, readable, evenly aligned, professional. No command names, no slash commands, no version numbers, no percentages.

three-clerks.prompt: Editorial flat-vector illustration on a soft cream (#FFF9F0) background with paper grain, navy (#2B3A67) linework, coral (#FF6B6B) and sunshine-yellow (#FFE66D) accents. Title across the top in bold navy: 'THE THREE CLERKS'. Three friendly desk clerks side by side at three cream counters, each with a hanging navy sign above. Left counter, sign 'CODE': a tidy clerk made of a simple calculator-and-ruler robot, stamping forms mechanically fast, caption below 'rules, math, dates — free and instant'. Middle counter, sign 'JEV', the largest and central: Frankie404 (see mascot spec) in a navy customs officer cap, holding a rubber stamp, a small confidence meter on the counter glowing yellow, a stack of document cards being sorted into CLEARED and SECONDARY trays, caption below 'narrow judgment over text — a snap answer with a confidence'. Right counter, sign 'LLM': a thoughtful clerk shaped like a large friendly owl-lamp with reading glasses and a quill, writing a long letter, a thinking cloud overhead, caption below 'reasoning, writing, taste — slow and expensive'. Small arrows show items flowing from left to right: simple ones stop at CODE, most stop at JEV, the few hard ones reach LLM. Bottom line in navy: 'Every step goes to one of the three.' Clean, balanced, legible, warm. No slash commands, no version numbers, no prices, no percentages.
